Subject: Effective-rate walkthrough + guardrails for per-token ladder

Hi Jatin,

Thanks again for taking time today. Per our call, I attached two artifacts: a short SOW draft and a lightweight breakpoint model that illustrates how monthly token shapes map to effective (blended) rates under a strictly marginal ladder. 

Quick notes to prime the conversation:
- The ladder in tab A is purely marginal: each TB (breakpoint) price applies only to tokens inside that band.
- Tab B shows a blended effective rate if you were to average across forecasted monthly usage (useful for finance comparisons).
- We added a safety cap for burst months (soft cap that triggers first to avoid unexpected bill shocks).

Could you confirm:
1) Your expected monthly token distribution (p50, p75, peak) for Q2–Q4?
2) Any procurement constraints around term minimums or billing calendars (monthly vs. quarterly)?

I'll loop in Marcus (discount desk) and Aditya (sales engineering) on the next note so we can align the margin/latency trade-offs if you prefer a lower marginal breakpoint in exchange for pinned capacity.

Best,

Hi Neha,

Thanks — reviewed the two attachments quickly. A couple of clarifying questions from procurement and finance:

1) We prefer a blended effective rate for our CFO reporting. If you provide us both marginal and blended summaries per quarter, that should work.
2) For contract term: our default is annual with quarterly invoicing, but we need a 60-day termination notice window (is that acceptable?).
3) Regarding the safety cap, is that a hard throttle or just an invoicing guard that triggers a credit discussion? We want predictable SLA behavior for top-tier customers.

Also, our expected token shape for Q2 (rough): p50 = 250M tokens/mo, p75 = 420M, peak = 900M. We can share a CSV.

Jatin

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.example.com>

Cc: Jatin Patel <procurement@acme.com>, Aisha Rani <aisha.rani@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Effective-rate walkthrough + guardrails for per-token ladder — internal alignment

Folks,

Looping you both in — ACME sent their rough token shape (p50/p75/peak above). Procurement wants blended numbers for CFO reporting and is asking about the safety cap semantics and termination notice (60-day).

Options I see:
- Option A (marginal ladder, no committed capacity): lower list marginal prices, but effective blended rate depends heavily on volume shape. Could be messy for finance reporting.
- Option B (committed band with blended guarantee): ACME commits to a soft minimum for Q2–Q4; we offer a blended effective floor and slightly improved marginals. Requires billing/commit language — Marcus help on the wording.
- Option C (hybrid): commit to a baseline monthly minimum + overage marginal ladder + a hard burst cap with pre-approved burst credits.

Marcus — can you outline the financial/legal guardrails we need for Option B vs C? Specifically: billing cadence (quarterly ok), termination window (we can accept 60 days if we add an early termination fee tied to unused committed tokens), and how to operationalize the burst cap (metric + alert + auto-credit).
Aditya — can you note latency/throughput implications if we pin a portion of dedicated capacity for ACME? They care about SLA.

Thanks — I’ll consolidate and send a revised SOW + example calc.

-Neha

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.example.com>
To: Jatin Patel <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Aisha Rani <aisha.rani@acme.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Updated proposal: blended summary + optional commit band (summary + next steps)

Hi Jatin / Aisha,

Thanks again for the prompt answers — based on your volume shape and our internal guidance, attached is a single-page summary that includes:
- A Q2–Q4 blended effective-rate table (works for CFO reporting).
- A marginal ladder for overages (transparent per-band pricing).
- Two optional commercial paths:
  • Path 1 (No commit): Marginal ladder only + soft safety cap (invoicing guard, not hard throttle).
  • Path 2 (Committed band): ACME commits to a baseline monthly token volume (e.g., 300M/mo averaged over the quarter). We offer a blended effective-rate guarantee and a 10% rebate for unused committed tokens applied quarterly, plus a reduced marginal overage price. Early termination: 60-day notice with a pro-rated commitment shortfall fee (simple formula included).

Operational notes:
- Safety cap behavior: soft cap triggers an automated notification and places excess usage into a review queue; invoicing will capture overages at the marginal rate, but our CS team will proactively engage for credits in the event of a platform incident. For enterprise SLA requests, we can discuss reserved capacity (Dedicated) as part of Path 2.
- Billing cadence: quarterly invoicing (we can do monthly if needed).

Next steps:
1) If Path 2 looks reasonable, we’ll produce a redlineable SOW (attached).
2) If you want a deterministic blended rate for internal reporting now, confirm which forecast column (p50 vs p75) to use and we’ll provide the one-line blended figure.

I attached: redwood-draft-sow.pdf (SOW template) and acme-usage-breakpoint-model.xlsx (calculator).

Would love to get a short call Thursday to close commercial approach — propose Thu 21 Jan 10:00 PT or 14:00 PT.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
